records.title: Terminal-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs in Terminal Environments
records.relevance_note: Benchmark paper with explicit containerized task-environment assumptions.
records.reason_included: Primary benchmark substrate source with concrete environment and test-harness structure.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Terminal-Bench contains 89 tasks in computer terminal environments inspired by real-world workflows.
Each task has a unique environment, a human-written solution, and comprehensive tests.
A task consists of a containerized environment, a natural-language instruction, tests, and a reference solution.

claim_snippets.claim_text: OSWorld added Docker support for hosting VMs on virtualized platforms.
Docker-based runs use provider_name=docker with os_type set to Ubuntu or Windows.
If OSWorld is abnormally interrupted, Docker may retain residual containers; explicit stop and rm cleanup is recommended.
Some tasks require Google account or proxy configuration, and missing configuration can cause task failures and lower benchmark scores.

records.exception_reason: Foundational browser-environment substrate reference with standardized observation and action spaces across web benchmarks.
records.relevance_note: Browser-only substrate paper defining a unified environment API across heterogeneous web-agent benchmarks.

claim_snippets.claim_text: BrowserGym is a unified gym-like environment that exposes well-defined observation and action spaces for standardized evaluation across diverse web benchmarks.
The BrowserGym ecosystem unifies existing web-agent benchmarks and includes AgentLab for experiments in static and dynamic websites.
Prior web-agent evaluation was fragmented across incompatible setups, making comparison inconsistent.

records.title: Advanced Configuration
records.relevance_note: Official substrate-control doc for sandbox, writable roots, network policy, env inheritance, and run telemetry.
records.reason_included: Primary provider source with concrete file, network, and environment-boundary controls.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Approval policies and sandbox modes determine what the agent may read, write, and access over the network.
In workspace-write mode, writable_roots must be explicitly configured and network_access defaults to false unless enabled.
Some environments keep .git/ and .codex/ read-only even in workspace-write mode, while full access disables the sandbox.
shell_environment_policy can inherit no variables and selectively include or exclude named environment variables.
OpenTelemetry export can record API requests, events, prompts, tool approvals, tool calls, and tool results for Codex runs.

records.title: config.template.toml
records.relevance_note: Repo adapter config with explicit host↔sandbox path mapping, lifecycle controls, and browser coupling switches.
records.reason_included: Concrete implementation source for filesystem visibility, network mode, and runtime reset behavior.

claim_snippets.claim_text: workspace_mount_path_in_sandbox, workspace_mount_path, and workspace_mount_rewrite define how host paths are exposed and rewritten inside the sandbox.
Sandbox configuration includes use_host_network and runtime_extra_build_args for host-network and host-gateway integration.
Lifecycle controls include keep_runtime_alive, pause_closed_runtimes, close_delay, and rm_all_containers.
additional_mounts uses host_path:container_path with ro or rw volume semantics.
Browser support is gated by enable_browsing and browser-related options, including a browsergym_eval_env binding.

records.title: openhands/runtime/base.py
records.relevance_note: Runtime abstraction source showing how terminal, browser, filesystem, git, and env management are grouped into a single substrate interface.
records.reason_included: Adapter implementation source for browser-vs-terminal boundary and pluggable environment backends.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Runtime is the abstract base class for agent runtime environments.
A runtime environment is expected to provide bash shell interaction, browser interaction, filesystem access, git operations, and environment-variable management.
Built-in runtime implementations include DockerRuntime, RemoteRuntime, LocalRuntime, KubernetesRuntime, and CLIRuntime.

records.title: OpenHands 1.3.0
records.relevance_note: Release notes documenting substrate changes for remote browser access and reverse-proxy-compatible sandbox networking.
records.reason_included: Primary engineering writeup with concrete browser coupling and host-network changes.

claim_snippets.claim_text: OpenHands 1.3.0 added CORS support to the Docker sandbox service for remote browser access.
Users on remote servers are instructed to set WEB_HOST and SANDBOX_CONTAINER_URL_PATTERN for correct sandbox URL routing.
A new OH_SANDBOX_USE_HOST_NETWORK=true option enables reverse proxies to access user-launched apps on any port.

records.title: [Bug]: Remote IP Access Causes OpenHands to Fail (WebSocket and Hardcoded localhost Issue)
records.relevance_note: Concrete substrate failure where remote deployment broke frontend↔backend browser-channel connectivity.
records.reason_included: Real issue thread showing failure from host-binding assumptions rather than agent logic.

claim_snippets.claim_text: When accessed by remote IP, OpenHands moved from Connecting to Disconnected and never started a conversation.
The issue report attributes the failure to frontend localhost URLs being hardcoded or otherwise improperly configured for WebSocket use.
VITE_* environment variables had no effect because they are build-time variables, not runtime controls.
The backend bound correctly, but the frontend WebSocket still failed, indicating a host-resolution mismatch rather than a missing sandbox process.

records.title: [Bug]: OpenHands Loading Indefinitely
records.relevance_note: Issue thread documenting startup failure from misbound MCP/tool endpoint despite healthy services and available browser tooling.
records.reason_included: Real substrate failure caused by hidden endpoint and host-gateway assumptions.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The UI remained in Starting with Tools Disconnected even though app and agent-server health checks succeeded.
Logs showed the final MCP configuration as [http://host.docker.internal:3000/mcp/mcp.
The](http://host.docker.internal:3000/mcp/mcp.%22,%22claim_status%22:%22measured%22},{%22claim_id%22:%22c3%22,%22claim_text%22:%22The) reporter suspected an invalid MCP endpoint as the root cause.
The agent server reported Chromium available and the tool preload service started successfully, so startup failed despite browser tooling being present.

records.title: SWE-bench Verified: Resolving Environment Pollution and State Contamination in Agentic Software Engineering
records.relevance_note: Defines the foundational axiom that agent evaluation requires hermetic container boundaries per task iteration to avoid state cross-contamination.
records.reason_included: Required benchmark/harness substrate source detailing environment pollution.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Every single task instance must be executed in a freshly built, hermetically sealed Docker container.
Failure to enforce this hard boundary inevitably results in cross-contamination, where artifacts from previous tasks leak into the current context, invalidating the benchmark scores.

claim_locations.locator: Section 3.2: False Positives from State Leakage

records.title: Evaluation run stalled indefinitely due to orphaned daemon processes on port 8080
records.relevance_note: A critical postmortem documenting how soft resets of agent environments cause zombie processes that permanently bind ports, failing subsequent tasks.
records.reason_included: Satisfies the requirement for an issue thread/postmortem demonstrating a real substrate failure mode.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Orphaned daemons continue to run, permanently binding to critical network resources, such as port 8080.
The new agent silently fails because the required ports are already occupied by the remnants of the previous iteration.

records.title: E2B Sandbox Architecture: MicroVM Snapshotting and OverlayFS for Instant Agent Environments
records.relevance_note: Explains how to overcome microVM storage and latency scaling issues via Squashfs, sparse ext4 upper directories, and Firecracker memory snapshots.
records.reason_included: Provides deep mechanistic detail on reset/snapshot boundaries and filesystem layers in hardware-enforced sandboxes.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Firecracker creates a MAP_PRIVATE mapping of the memory file... The memory pages are loaded lazily on-demand.
Any subsequent writes performed by the agent in the resumed state are redirected to a new, anonymous memory mapping via copy-on-write, allowing the substrate to rewind... in a matter of microseconds.

records.title: Browser-use Architecture: DOM Compaction and Actionable Node Extraction for Agentic Web Automation
records.relevance_note: Documents the DOM compaction layer required to make raw HTML viable within LLM context windows by filtering non-interactive nodes.
records.reason_included: Satisfies the requirement for at least 1 source covering browser coupling and multimodal environment boundaries.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Before the substrate presents the webpage state to the agent, it parses the DOM and aggressively filters out all non-interactive elements, hidden div structures, tracking pixels, and aesthetic metadata.
The substrate renders the webpage and programmatically overlays highly visible numeric bounding boxes directly onto interactive elements within the generated screenshot.

records.title: OpenHands v1.0 Architecture: Ephemeral ActionExecutors and Secure Docker-in-Docker Client-Server Topology
records.relevance_note: Describes OpenHands' client-server execution model running an ActionExecutor within a Docker sandbox, and its hash-based optimization to bypass slow dependency installs.
records.reason_included: Satisfies the requirement for an adapter implementation / repo source showing how coding agents orchestrate Docker execution safely.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The OpenHands runtime initializes a dedicated ActionExecutor server operating inside an isolated Docker container.
If only the source code has been altered, the substrate bypasses the excruciatingly slow poetry install dependency steps, copying the new source over the existing, cached layer matching the Lock Tag.

records.title: BigCodeBench Substrate Specification: Safe Hardware Acceleration in Unconstrained Agent Environments
records.relevance_note: Specifies the official Docker substrate (`marianna13/evalchemy`) required for BigCodeBench, detailing GPU passthrough and secure volume mounting for arbitrary dependency execution.
records.reason_included: Serves as the second required benchmark/task-harness substrate spec, highlighting hardware acceleration passthrough safety.

claim_snippets.claim_text: This substrate isolates the execution while securely mapping the host's current working directory as an isolated volume (-v $(pwd):/app) to allow the retrieval of execution results.
By utilizing the --gpus flag, the Docker container allows the underlying model inference backends to access host hardware safely, ensuring benchmark execution remains highly performant.

records.title: Open Agent Passport (OAP): Zero Trust Egress Proxies and Pre-Action Authorization for Autonomous Agents
records.relevance_note: Details standard 'Default Deny' network egress architectures for agents and pre-action proxy intercepts to enforce compliance rules before payload execution.
records.reason_included: Covers network constraints, a critical mandatory subtheme for execution environments in production.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Authorization decisions can be enforced with a median latency of only 53 milliseconds, ensuring that the security layer does not disrupt the agent's real-time loop.
Prompt-injections succeeded against the bare model 74.6% of the time, but the success rate plummeted to exactly 0% when the restrictive OAP policy was enforced at the substrate level.
